html:
Lysistrata is a comedy by Aristophanes, first staged in Athens early in 411 BCE. Its heroine persuades the women of the warring Greek cities to refuse sex to their husbands until the men make peace.

Her name means "army disbander". She brings together women from Athens, Sparta and other cities, and the older women seize the Acropolis, where the city's war funds are kept. A chorus of old men tries to smoke them out and is drenched by a chorus of old women. In the end the desperate men of both sides give in and make peace, and the play closes with feasting and dancing.

The joke had a serious edge. The play came after the disaster of the Sicilian Expedition, with the Peloponnesian War in its twentieth year, and just months before the oligarchic coup. It is the best known of his plays today and is often staged as an anti-war comedy. In 2003, readings of it were held around the world in protest against the coming Iraq War.
sum: Lysistrata is a comedy by Aristophanes, first staged in Athens early in 411 BCE. Its heroine persuades the women of the warring Greek cities to refuse sex to their husbands until the men make peace.
